subject: economics
topic: Economic organisations (ECOWAS, AU, OPEC, IMF, World Bank)

kept.q: In what year was the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) established?
kept.explanation: ECOWAS was formed in 1975 through the Treaty of Lagos, signed by West African countries to promote economic co-operation and integration in the sub-region.
kept.pidgin: Na for 1975 dem form ECOWAS, through di Treaty of Lagos, make West African kontri dem fit work together for economy matter.

kept.q: OPEC is an acronym that stands for which of the following?
options: Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries
Organisation for Promoting Export Co-operation
Organisation of Palm-oil Exporting Countries
Organisation of Pan-African Economic Co-operation
kept.explanation: OPEC means the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, a body formed by major oil-producing nations to coordinate and unify petroleum policies.
kept.pidgin: OPEC na Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, na di kontri wey dey produce crude oil come form am to arrange dia oil policy together.

kept.q: The headquarters of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is located in which city?
options: Accra, Ghana
Lagos, Nigeria
Abuja, Nigeria
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
kept.explanation: ECOWAS has its secretariat headquarters in Abuja, Nigeria, after it moved from Lagos when Nigeria changed its capital city.
kept.pidgin: ECOWAS headquarters dey Abuja, Nigeria, dem move am from Lagos come Abuja after Nigeria change im capital.

kept.q: A member country of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is experiencing a severe shortage of foreign exchange needed to pay for essential imports. Which type of assistance would the IMF most likely provide to this country?
options: A long-term loan to build new industries
A short-term loan to correct the balance of payments problem
A grant to fund free education for its citizens
A permanent subsidy on all its exports
kept.explanation: The IMF's main role is to give short-term financial support to countries facing balance of payments difficulties, unlike the World Bank, which gives long-term development loans.
kept.pidgin: IMF dey give short-term loan to kontri wey dey find am hard to balance dia foreign payment, e no be im work to build industry or give free school money, na World Bank dey do long-term loan.

kept.q: Which of the following best describes the main function of the World Bank?
options: It provides long-term loans for development projects such as roads, dams and schools
It sets production quotas for crude oil among member states
It settles political disputes between African countries
It issues a common currency for its member countries
kept.explanation: The World Bank mainly gives long-term loans to developing countries to fund infrastructure and development projects like roads, power plants and schools.
kept.pidgin: World Bank dey give long-term loan make kontri fit build road, dam, school and odas, e no be oil quota matter or political wahala be dia work.

kept.q: The African Union (AU) has its headquarters in which city?
options: Abuja, Nigeria
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
Accra, Ghana
Cairo, Egypt
kept.explanation: The African Union, which replaced the Organisation of African Unity, has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
kept.pidgin: African Union headquarters dey Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, na dis organisation replace di old OAU.

kept.q: In the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a member country's voting power is determined mainly by the size of its financial quota contribution. If Nigeria contributes a larger quota to the IMF than another member country, what is the most likely outcome?
options: Nigeria will have greater voting power than that country
Both countries will automatically have equal voting rights
The other country will have greater voting power than Nigeria
Voting power has nothing to do with quota size
kept.explanation: In the IMF, voting power is linked directly to a country's quota contribution; the bigger the quota a country pays, the greater its voting strength in IMF decisions. Since Nigeria's quota is larger, it will enjoy greater voting power than the other country.
kept.pidgin: For IMF, di money (quota) wey kontri put dey decide how much vote dem go get; bigger quota mean bigger vote. So if Nigeria quota pass di oda kontri own, Nigeria go get more vote pass dem.
